query: Consider the following context: High entropy alloys have excellent wear resistance, so they have great application prospects in the fields of wear resistance and surface protection. In that context, which material can be used for adhere to the surface of a Cu matrix, and why?

generation.hypothesis: The addition of alloying elements such as Cr, Ti, or Nb to a High Entropy Alloy (HEA) can enhance its adhesion to a Cu matrix, thereby improving wear resistance and surface protection.
generation.material_initial_state: High Entropy Alloy (HEA) in its initial composition
generation.intervention: Addition of alloying elements (e.g., Cr, Ti, or Nb) to the HEA
generation.conditions: The HEA is adhered to the surface of a Cu matrix
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a strong interface between the HEA and the Cu matrix due to alloying and solid solution strengthening
generation.mechanism: Alloying and solid solution strengthening mechanisms enhance the adhesion and wear resistance of the HEA on the Cu matrix
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved adhesion and wear resistance of the HEA on the Cu matrix
generation.baseline: The initial wear resistance and adhesion of the HEA on the Cu matrix without the addition of alloying elements
generation.boundary: The maximum amount of alloying elements that can be added without compromising the structural integrity of the HEA
generation.uncertainty: The optimal composition and amount of alloying elements required to achieve the best adhesion and wear resistance, as well as the potential effects on the microstructure and mechanical properties of the HEA

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare samples of HEA with varying amounts of alloying elements (e.g., Cr, Ti, or Nb) and adhere them to a Cu matrix. Measure the adhesion strength and wear resistance of each sample using standardized tests (e.g., scratch test, pin-on-disk test).
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the addition of alloying elements does not result in a significant improvement in adhesion and wear resistance, the hypothesis is falsified.
